questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If $A - B = \frac{\pi}{4}$, then $(1+\tan A)(1-\tan B)$ is equal to:

explanation.summary: $\tan(A-B) = 1 \implies \frac{\tan A - \tan B}{1+\tan A\tan B} = 1 \implies \tan A - \tan B - \tan A\tan B = 1$. Thus $(1+\tan A)(1-\tan B) = 1 + \tan A - \tan B - \tan A\tan B = 1 + 1 = 2$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: $\tan(A-B) = 1 \implies \frac{\tan A - \tan B}{1+\tan A\tan B} = 1 \implies \tan A - \tan B - \tan A\tan B = 1$. Thus $(1+\tan A)(1-\tan B) = 1 + \tan A - \tan B - \tan A\tan B = 1 + 1 = 2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: Let $P(E)$ denote the probability of event $E$. Given $P(A) = 1, P(B) = 1/2$, the values of $P(A|B)$ and $P(B|A)$ respectively are:

explanation.summary: Since $P(A)=1$, $A$ is certain event, so $P(A \cap B) = P(B) = 1/2$. Thus $P(A|B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} = 1$, and $P(B|A) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(A)} = \frac{1/2}{1} = 1/2$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: Since $P(A)=1$, $A$ is certain event, so $P(A \cap B) = P(B) = 1/2$. Thus $P(A|B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} = 1$, and $P(B|A) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(A)} = \frac{1/2}{1} = 1/2$.

questions.questionText: The number of values of $k$ for which the system $(k+1)x + 8y = 4k$ and $kx + (k+3)y = 3k-1$ has infinitely many solutions is:

explanation.summary: For infinite solutions: $\frac{k+1}{k} = \frac{8}{k+3} = \frac{4k}{3k-1}$. $(k+1)(k+3) = 8k \implies k^2 - 4k + 3 = 0 \implies k = 1, 3$. For $k=3$: $8/6 = 4/3$ and $\frac{4(3)}{3(3)-1} = 12/8 = 3/2 \ne 4/3$. For $k=1$: $\frac{1+1}{1} = 2, \frac{8}{1+3} = 2, \frac{4(1)}{3(1)-1} = 2$. Thus only $k=1$ satisfies (1 value).

For $k=3$: $8/6 = 4/3$ and $\frac{4(3)}{3(3)-1} = 12/8 = 3/2 \ne 4/3$. For $k=1$: $\frac{1+1}{1} = 2, \frac{8}{1+3} = 2, \frac{4(1)}{3(1)-1} = 2$. Thus only $k=1$ satisfies (1 value).

explanation.summary: Determinant of components: $\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & \lambda & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\lambda - 1 \end{vmatrix} = 1 \cdot \lambda(2\lambda - 1)$.
